issue_context.title: A Plugwise integration gets discovered while there already is a Plugwise integration present.
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Several users, myself included, report receiving a notification that a new Plugwise integration has been discovered while there is (are) an existing Plugwise integration(s).

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.113.0
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.112.0 
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): 
- Integration causing this issue: Plugwise
- Link to integration documentation on our website:
comments:
Hey there @compatech, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`plugwise`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L317) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

This error is probably caused because different config_flow unique_ids are used by the zeroconf discovery process versus the manual entry process.

We think this can be fixed by using the same unique_id in both the zeroconf discovery process and the manual entry process, is that correct? 
We have a solution for this but this will most likely be a breaking change. 
Should we implement this change, or not? 
Please advise @frenck @bdraco

> This error is probably caused because different config_flow unique_ids are used by the zeroconf discovery process versus the manual entry process.
> 
> We think this can be fixed by using the same unique_id in both the zeroconf discovery process and the manual entry process, is that correct?
> We have a solution for this but this will most likely be a breaking change.
> Should we implement this change, or not?
> Please advise @frenck @bdraco

@bouwew 

The unique ids should be the same coming from zeroconf or manual setup.  You can migrate the existing config entries with `async_update_entry` to avoid making this a breaking change.

@bdraco we're testing with your suggestion. However, something strange is going on, I think: when I check the `entry.unique_id` in `__init__.py` (with header `async def async_setup_entry(hass, entry):`), it has the value `None`. While it just previously, when adding the integration, has been set to a specific value in config_flow.py.
I would expect the unique_id to have that specific value and not None, when checking its value in `__init__.py`, or am I wrong?

> @bdraco this is what I see in core.config_entries directly after adding the integration:
> 
> ```
> 
>             {
> 
>                 "connection_class": "local_poll",
> 
>                 "data": {
> 
>                     "host": "192.168.1.212",
> 
>                     "password": "cnbljxgd"
> 
>                 },
> 
>                 "domain": "plugwise-beta",
> 
>                 "entry_id": "053fc909163344489beb6ead8d1988c4",
> 
>                 "options": {},
> 
>                 "source": "user",
> 
>                 "system_options": {
> 
>                     "disable_new_entities": false
> 
>                 },
> 
>                 "title": "Adam",
> 
>                 "unique_id": null,
> 
>                 "version": 1
> 
>             }
> 
> ```
> 
> 
> 
> Can this be because I'm testing with my custom_component? Instead of with the Core version of Plugwise?
> 
> 
> 
> Also, something else, while trying to debug, I've noticed that the debugging-messages from config_flow.py are no longer present in Logs. The debugging- and other kind of logger-messages from `__init__.py`, climate.py, sensor.py, etc are still shown but the logger-messages from config_flow.py are no longer there. Do you want me to create a separate Issue for this?

Looks like it was created without a unique id from your testing.

What is your logger configuration set to?

Update: looks like I'm having a conflict: I'm trying to use Plugwise_Smile v1.2.0 in the custom_component but it gets overwritten by v1.1.0 which is the default for Core Plugwise. Better not to mix production and testing :|

@bdraco we are setting the unique_id like in other integrations:
```
            if not errors:
                unique_id = api.gateway_id
                if api.hostname is not None:
                    unique_id = api.hostname
                _LOGGER.debug("Unique_id is set to: %s", unique_id)
                await self.async_set_unique_id(unique_id)
                self._abort_if_unique_id_configured()

                return self.async_create_entry(title=api.smile_name, data=user_input)
```

I tried to debug this code but no debug messages from config_flow.py shown in Logs anymore.

My logger-config looks like:
```
logger:
  default: warn
  logs:
    homeassistant.components.brother: fatal
    custom_components.plugwise-beta: debug
```

> Update: looks like I'm having a conflict: I'm trying to use Plugwise_Smile v1.2.0 in the custom_component but it gets overwritten by v1.1.0 which is the default for Core Plugwise. Better not to mix production and testing :|
> 

If you update name your `custom_component` the same as the `core` name and update `manifest.json` in the `custom_component`, it should overwrite the version.

> @bdraco we are setting the unique_id like in other integrations:
> 
> ```
>             if not errors:
>                 unique_id = api.gateway_id
>                 if api.hostname is not None:
>                     unique_id = api.hostname
>                 _LOGGER.debug("Unique_id is set to: %s", unique_id)
>                 await self.async_set_unique_id(unique_id)
>                 self._abort_if_unique_id_configured()
> 
>                 return self.async_create_entry(title=api.smile_name, data=user_input)
> ```
> 
> I tried to debug this code but no debug messages from config_flow.py shown in Logs anymore.
> 
> My logger-config looks like:
> 
> ```
> logger:
>   default: warn
>   logs:
>     homeassistant.components.brother: fatal
>     custom_components.plugwise-beta: debug
> ```

That looks right.  Can you try naming it the same and using `custom_components.plugwise` ?

Ah yes, why do I keep forgetting that stuff!

BTW, I've modified our code a bit, the unique_id-part is now fully working in my test-environment.

Wrt the logger, I'll try your suggestion, let you know the result.

@bdraco I'm seeing the _LOGGER-messages from config_flow now :)

Thanks for helping, very much appreciated!

review_comments: Is the smile host name the same as the gateway id?
For some older devices the smile_hostname isn't amongst the data so for cases where it would end up `None` we use the gateway_id (which is sort of an internal string/hash).
Ok, so the same device will always use the same unique id.
Why are we setting unique id again here if we're coming from the zeroconf step? Will we use the same unique id then as was set in the zeroconf step?

Some people can't use zeroconf for some reason, so we are setting the same unique_id here.
Yes, it's the same as in the zeroconf-step.
Does this mean that some devices or entries won't get a unique id?

No, this means that for some devices the unique_id will not be updated.
But for these devices we have changed nothing, still using `gateway_id`, so there should not be any issue.
But these entries will still not have a unique id. I guess the same host check in the config flow should guard from setting up these again.

Yes they were given a unique_id before and we are still giving these devices the same unique_id with the updated code.
These are the only Plugwise devices that cannot be discovered via zeroconf (we think, we don't have contact with a user that has one). So nothing has been changed for these devices.
